checks.covers: An AI reading of the logging setup and of the log calls for the metadata each entry carries (time, place, actor, event).
checks.misses: What the log lines look like at run time, formatting added by the logging platform, and code the model did not read.

entries.why: Whether an entry carries enough metadata for an investigation depends on the logger's format and on each call site, a judgment no pattern makes.

checks.covers: Secrets written to logs and error messages.
checks.misses: Data that is allowed in logs only masked or hashed by protection level, and personal data.

checks.id: DATA-ISOLATION-AND-LIFECYCLE.md#Analytics, logs, traces, and diagnostics as alternate readers
checks.covers: Private content or credentials emitted into logs and traces readable by a broader audience.
checks.misses: Whether the application has a per-class logging policy to enforce.

checks.covers: A value or object key named like a password, token, secret or authorization header given to a console, winston, pino or bunyan style logging call.
checks.misses: Sensitive values under names the list does not hold, values logged after passing through a function, and personal data of any name.

checks.covers: A value named like a password, token or secret passed to a Python logging call.
checks.misses: Sensitive values under other names, values logged after passing through a function, and personal data of any name.

checks.covers: The Authorization header or a similar credential header of the request passed to a logging call.
checks.misses: Headers copied into another structure before logging, whole-request dumps, and other credential headers the rule does not name.

checks.covers: A value named like a password, token or secret passed to a C# logging call.
checks.misses: Sensitive values under other names, values logged after passing through a function, and personal data of any name.

checks.covers: The Authorization header of the request passed to a logging call.
checks.misses: Headers copied into another structure before logging, whole-request dumps, and other credential headers.

checks.covers: A value named like a password, token or secret passed to a Go logging call.
checks.misses: Sensitive values under other names, values logged after passing through a function, and personal data of any name.

checks.covers: A structured-logging field whose key is named like a password, token or secret.
checks.misses: Fields under other key names, values logged through a wrapper, and personal data of any name.

checks.covers: The Authorization header of the request passed to a logging call.
checks.misses: Headers copied into another structure before logging, whole-request dumps, and other credential headers.

checks.covers: A value named like a password, token or secret passed to SLF4J, Log4j, Logback, java.util.logging, commons-logging or System.out.
checks.misses: Sensitive values under other names, values logged after passing through a function, and personal data of any name.

checks.covers: The Authorization header of the request passed to a logging call.
checks.misses: Headers copied into another structure before logging, whole-request dumps, and other credential headers.

checks.covers: A value named like a password, token or secret passed to a PHP logging call.
checks.misses: Sensitive values under other names, values logged after passing through a function, and personal data of any name.

checks.covers: A value named like a password, token or secret given to a log or tracing macro, as an argument, a field value or inline in the format string.
checks.misses: Sensitive values under other names, values logged after passing through a function, and personal data of any name.

entries.why: Both audit blocks look for sensitive values reaching logs, and the rules name the credential-named value in a logging call in each language, which is the violation this item forbids when the name gives it away.

checks.covers: An AI reading of the login, logout and credential-check paths for a log entry on success and on failure, with the type of authentication.
checks.misses: Authentication done by an identity provider or a gateway outside the repository, and what the logs hold at run time.

entries.why: Whether every authentication path logs both outcomes is a question about the presence of a call in many places, which a model can read and a pattern cannot decide.

checks.covers: An AI reading of the authorization checks and their failure branches for a log entry when access is refused.
checks.misses: Denials made by a gateway or framework layer outside the repository, and logging of every decision or of sensitive-data access at the higher assurance levels.

entries.why: The presence of a log call on each refusal branch is a judgment over the authorization code, which the AI review can examine.

checks.covers: An AI reading of input validation, business-rule and anti-automation checks for a log entry when a request fails them.
checks.misses: Which security events the project documents, bypass attempts seen only at run time, and controls outside the repository.

entries.why: Whether rejected requests leave a trace depends on each control's failure branch, read in context against what the project calls a security event.

checks.covers: Empty catch blocks and empty promise catch handlers in JavaScript and TypeScript, where an error is dropped with no log.
checks.misses: Handlers that do something unrelated to logging, errors dropped through a wrapper, and security control failures that raise no exception.

checks.covers: Python handlers that catch an exception and drop it with no log, rethrow or handling.
checks.misses: Handlers that do something unrelated to logging, errors dropped through a wrapper, and control failures that raise no exception.

checks.covers: Empty broad catch blocks in C#, where the error is dropped with no log.
checks.misses: Narrow handlers that drop errors, handlers with unrelated statements, and control failures that raise no exception.

checks.covers: Go error checks whose branch drops the error with no log, handling or return.
checks.misses: Errors assigned to a name and never checked, branches with unrelated statements, and control failures that return no error.

checks.covers: Java catch blocks that drop the exception with no log, handling or rethrow; a variable named ignored marks a deliberate choice.
checks.misses: Handlers with unrelated statements, errors dropped through a wrapper, and control failures that raise no exception.

checks.covers: PHP catch blocks that drop the exception with no log, handling or rethrow.
checks.misses: Handlers with unrelated statements, errors dropped through a wrapper, and control failures that raise no exception.

entries.why: An error that is caught and dropped is never logged, which is the direct opposite of this item. The rules see the empty handler, not a handler that logs poorly or a security failure that never throws.

checks.covers: Untrusted input reaching logging and other secondary systems, log injection among the sinks listed.
checks.misses: The logging components' own encoding behaviour; the block treats logs as one sink among many.

entries.why: The injection block lists log injection as a sink to trace, which is what this item asks to prevent.

checks.covers: Stack traces, driver messages and verbose errors written into responses.
checks.misses: Errors produced by frameworks or proxies configured outside the repository.

checks.covers: An error's stack written through an Express or Fastify style response call.
checks.misses: Stacks put into a variable first, other response APIs, and a framework's own debug error page.

checks.covers: An error's stack assigned to the Koa response body.
checks.misses: Stacks put into a variable first, other response APIs, and a framework's own debug error page.

checks.covers: An exception's message written through a response call, where internal detail such as a query or a path can reach the caller.
checks.misses: Messages built from the error before sending, generic messages that still hold detail, and other response APIs.

checks.covers: Python tracebacks or formatted exception traces written into an HTTP response.
checks.misses: Traces placed in a variable first, a debug mode that renders them, and other response APIs.

checks.covers: An exception's text written into an HTTP response.
checks.misses: Messages built from the exception before sending, and generic messages that still hold detail.

checks.covers: An exception's stack trace written into the HTTP response.
checks.misses: Traces placed in a variable first, the developer exception page enabled by configuration, and other response APIs.

checks.covers: An exception's message written into the HTTP response.
checks.misses: Messages built from the exception before sending, and generic messages that still hold detail.

checks.covers: A stack trace written to an HTTP response writer.
checks.misses: Traces placed in a variable first, and response paths of frameworks the rule does not model.

checks.covers: An error's text written to an HTTP response writer.
checks.misses: Messages built from the error before sending, and generic messages that still hold detail.

checks.covers: A stack trace written through the servlet response, Spring or JAX-RS response objects.
checks.misses: Traces put into a variable first, and the container's own error page.

checks.covers: printStackTrace into the response writer.
checks.misses: Traces put into a variable first, and the container's own error page.

checks.covers: An exception's message written into the HTTP response.
checks.misses: Messages built from the exception before sending, and generic messages that still hold detail.

checks.covers: A stack trace written into the PHP response output.
checks.misses: Traces put into a variable first, and display_errors settings outside the code.

checks.covers: An exception's message written into the PHP response output.
checks.misses: Messages built from the exception before sending, and generic messages that still hold detail.

checks.covers: Framework configuration files that switch error detail on for the client (display_errors, custom errors mode, include-stacktrace and the like).
checks.misses: Settings passed by environment variable or command line, and values that differ between environments.

checks.covers: Error pages of a running instance that disclose application errors or debug messages, found by ZAP's passive checks on the pages its crawl or spec reached.
checks.misses: Everything only a deployed system shows beyond those pages: error paths ZAP never provoked, content behind logins it could not use, and what a proxy rewrites.

entries.why: The method category and the rules find error detail written into responses in source and in framework configuration; the ZAP check finds what the running pages return. The ZAP identifiers are the alert references of the report (the pluginid of ZAP's application error disclosure and debug error message rules, whose alert reference is not suffixed), matched exactly against the stage's findings.

checks.covers: axios requests made without a timeout, so the failure of an external resource is never signalled to the caller.
checks.misses: Other HTTP clients, a timeout set by a shared factory, and the fallback behaviour (circuit breaker, degraded response) after a failure.

checks.covers: Outbound HTTP calls of the common Python clients made without a timeout.
checks.misses: A timeout set on a session or wrapper elsewhere, and the fallback behaviour after a failure.

checks.covers: Go HTTP clients and calls built without a timeout.
checks.misses: A deadline carried by a context, a shared client built elsewhere, and the fallback behaviour after a failure.

checks.covers: Java outbound clients built or used without a timeout.
checks.misses: Timeouts set through a shared bean or container, and the fallback behaviour after a failure.

checks.covers: PHP outbound HTTP calls made without a timeout option.
checks.misses: A timeout in the client's shared configuration, and the fallback behaviour after a failure.

checks.covers: reqwest clients and calls built without a timeout.
checks.misses: A timeout set outside the same expression, and the fallback behaviour after a failure.

entries.why: A call with no timeout cannot fail in time, which blocks any graceful behaviour when an external resource stops answering. The rules see this precondition only; circuit breakers and degraded modes are outside what a pattern shows.

checks.covers: Empty catch blocks and promise handlers in JavaScript and TypeScript, where the code goes on as if nothing failed.
checks.misses: Handlers with statements that still let the flow continue unsafely, and fail-open logic written without any exception.

checks.covers: Python handlers that drop the exception and let execution continue.
checks.misses: Handlers with statements that still let the flow continue unsafely, and fail-open logic written without any exception.

checks.covers: Empty broad catch blocks in C#, where the code goes on after the failure.
checks.misses: Narrow handlers with the same effect, and fail-open logic written without any exception.

checks.covers: Go error checks whose branch drops the error, so the code goes on after the failure.
checks.misses: Errors never checked, errors checked but handled in an unsafe way, and fail-open logic written without any error value.

checks.covers: Java catch blocks that drop the exception, so the code goes on after the failure.
checks.misses: Handlers with statements that still let the flow continue unsafely, and fail-open logic written without any exception.

checks.covers: PHP catch blocks that drop the exception, so the code goes on after the failure.
checks.misses: Handlers with statements that still let the flow continue unsafely, and fail-open logic written without any exception.

entries.why: A dropped error is the simplest way a flow goes on after a failed check, and the rules mark only the empty handler. Fail-open logic that raises no error, and what the code does after a validation fails, stay outside what a pattern shows.

checks.covers: Paths where an unhandled error or panic can end a shared process, the case a last-resort handler exists to stop.
checks.misses: Whether such a handler is registered at all (the block hunts the consequence, not the handler), and supervisors outside the repository.

checks.covers: An AI reading of the application entry point and the framework setup for a global handler that catches what is left unhandled and logs it.
checks.misses: Handlers installed by the runtime, the platform or a supervisor outside the repository, and code the model did not read.

entries.why: The existence of one catch-all handler at the entry point is a fact about the application's wiring, which a model can read and no single pattern covers across frameworks.
